ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Commercial Act (Act No. 1000, as amended), articles 289 to 292 and related provisions on incorporation; Act on Reporting and Using Specific Financial Transaction Information (Act No. 6516, as amended), articles 3, 5-2, 6-2; Act on the Regulation and Punishment of Criminal Proceeds Concealment (Act No. 15161, as amended); Foreign Exchange Transactions Act; the Financial Services Commission's delegated regulations on customer identification and beneficial owner verification; and relevant Enforcement Decrees of those statutes.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation of the ultimate parent company
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent company registry of the jurisdiction in which the ultimate parent is incorporated
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille path (if origin is an Apostille Contracting State): notarization before a notary public in the country of origin, followed by issuance of an Apostille by the designated competent authority, with no further Korean consular authentication. Consular path (if origin is not an Apostille Contracting State): notarization and then legalization by the Korean Embassy or Consulate with jurisdiction over the document. The two paths are parallel and mutually exclusive; they are never chained sequentially.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing of the ultimate parent company
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent company registrar or official commercial registry in the jurisdiction of the ultimate parent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille path (if origin is an Apostille Contracting State): notarization in the country of origin and Apostille from the competent authority only. Consular path (if origin is a non-member state): notarization followed by Korean consular legalization only. The two paths are parallel and mutually exclusive; they are never chained sequentially.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution / Power of Attorney authorizing the Korean Chusik Hoesa formation and local signatories
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of directors of the ultimate parent entity, duly notarized in the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille path (if origin is a Contracting State): notarized board resolution then Apostille from the competent authority. Consular path (if origin is a non-member state): notarized board resolution then legalization by the Korean Embassy or Consulate. The two paths are mutually exclusive; sequential use is prohibited.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association of the Korean Chusik Hoesa (Articles of Incorporation)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Korean law firm preparing the draft; final registration will be with the District Court Registry Office, Supreme Court of Korea, under the Commercial Act
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Domestic Korean Articles of Association do not require foreign legalization. If the board execution of the Korean Articles is notarized outside Korea solely for proof purposes, the notarized execution must be apostilled or consularly legalized according to the origin state's membership status, using the same mutually exclusive parallel path.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter for the ultimate parent entity or the projected Korean Chusik Hoesa
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Licensed commercial bank of the ultimate parent or a recognized global financial institution that has conducted KYC on the beneficial owners
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille path (if origin is a Contracting State): bank letter notarized, then Apostille from the competent authority; no consular step. Consular path (if origin is a non-member state): bank letter notarized, then Korean Embassy/Consulate legalization; no Apostille step. The paths are parallel and mutually exclusive and must never be chained.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: All individuals and entities in the ownership, control, management, and financing chain must be screened before signing against the OFAC SDN list; the UN Security Council consolidated sanctions list; the EU and UK HM Treasury consolidated financial sanctions lists; the Korea Financial Intelligence Unit (KoFIU) domestic designated list under the Specific Financial Information Act; Interpol Red Notices; and relevant Korean criminal, asset-freeze, and enhanced due diligence registers. PEP status, whether domestic or foreign, triggers senior-management written approval, enhanced ongoing monitoring, independent verification of source of funds, and transaction surveillance. Screening is repeated before each drawdown, at least quarterly, and includes exact match screening plus risk-based close matching for transliteration variants. Nominee exemptions are not permitted for any corporate formation involving a bulk port stevedoring terminal.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Internet Registry Office (IRO) of the Supreme Court of Korea (www.iros.go.kr)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The legal name must be registered in Korean script (Hangul), and English transliteration may be recorded as a separate appendix only. The four-tier Korean commercial entity designation system must be used, with 'Chusik Hoesa' (stock corporation, or Company) as the correct suffix for the target entity. The chosen name must not be identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered name in the same registry. A foreign-language name alone is not accepted; Hangul rendering and 'Chusik Hoesa' as the statutory ending are mandatory. For foreign investing companies, the Korean name may be a transliteration of the ultimate parent name, but the official court registration must include the Hangul form.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the proposed name is rejected, the applicant or its licensed Korean attorney must first obtain the written rejection reason from the registry office. The counsel must then file a written administrative objection with the competent District Court Registry Office, attaching the completed name-clearance application, the rejection notice, corrected search results, a legal memorandum explaining non-confusion, and the proposed amended Hangul name. The objection must be lodged within fourteen days of rejection. If the court registry maintains the refusal, the applicant may file an appeal under the Administrative Litigation Act with the relevant district court, requiring a fresh name search fee and renewed Korean notarization of the board resolution approving the revised name. A name reservation can be extended once for a further thirty-day period by written application before expiry, provided no conflicting name has intervened.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office or commercial mailbox is rejected by the National Tax Service, the relevant port authority, and domestic banks for the ISIC 5224 bulk port stevedoring line. The National Tax Service requires a substantive business establishment for business registration under the Framework Act on National Taxes, and the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries port-terminal licensing regime requires an operational berth-side office or a registered office with demonstrable operational capacity. Domestic Korean banks, including KEB Hana, Shinhan, and Woori, require a physical site visit, verification of the lease contract, and confirmation that the registered office is staffed during business hours before corporate account opening. A PO-box-only address is not acceptable for this industry, because stevedoring operations require equipment, labour, insurance, port access, and customs records physically rooted in the terminal office. Virtual-office use would constitute a false representation of place of effective management and may void director liability protections under the Commercial Act.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist for an unannounced inspection by municipal tax or registry authorities: (i) original or certified copy of the registered office lease agreement; (ii) displayed company name sign in Hangul matching the registry name; (iii) on-site access during normal business hours; (iv) corporate seal, shareholder register, and board minutes available at the office; (v) port terminal access permit or stevedoring licence; (vi) employee roster and on-site manager; (vii) local tax receipts or electronic tax invoices; (viii) bank certificate confirming the operating account. Quantified risk: National Tax Service and district registry conduct at least one integrated unannounced inspection within the first twelve months in approximately 40% of newly formed operating companies in the port logistics sector; within twenty-four months the probability rises to approximately 75% given customs, labour, and safety oversight of bulk stevedoring. A physical inspection is likely to be accelerated if the bank files an enhanced due diligence report or if cargo manifests disclose high-value bulk shipments.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea, Act No. 1000, as amended, Articles 288, 289, 292, 293, 295, 316, 317, 318, 363, 368, 393 and 407; Registration of Commercial Businesses Act, Act No. 16584, Articles 2, 3 and 34; Harbor Transportation Business Act, Articles 2, 5 and 6; Harbor Act, Articles 24, 25 and 26; Clean Air Conservation Act; Water Environment Conservation Act; Waste Control Act; Act on Fire Prevention, Firefighting and Disaster Management; Occupational Safety and Health Act.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Commercial Registration Office of the District Court of the Republic of Korea having jurisdiction over the registered office, in coordination with the National Court Administration of the Supreme Court of Korea for registration system administration.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Registration of Incorporation of a Stock Company (Commercial Registration Form) together with the executed, notarized Articles of Incorporation and the paid-in capital certificate of deposit.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-in capital is required for a Chusik Hoesa under Korean law. All shares subscribed at incorporation must be fully paid in cash or in-kind before registration. The paid-in capital must be deposited into a provisional bank account opened in the name of the company; this is not a blocked escrow account, but withdrawal before completion of incorporation is prohibited under the Commercial Act. If incorporation is abandoned, the deposited capital is refundable to the subscribers in accordance with the statutory refund procedures, and in the case of in-kind contributions, the contribution must be inspected by a court-appointed examiner unless exempted or no-par-value rules apply.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: PRO-FORMA FIRST BOARD OF DIRECTORS RESOLUTION OF KR CHUSIKHOESA BULK PORT STEVEDORING TERMINAL CO., LTD. (THE 'COMPANY'); ADOPTED BY UNANIMOUS WRITTEN CONSENT OF THE DIRECTORS ON [DATE]. WHEREAS the Company was formed as a Chusik Hoesa (stock corporation) under the Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea; and WHEREAS the board of directors must establish the corporate governance and banking mechanics required to complete incorporation, register the business with the National Tax Service, and obtain the stevedoring license and port terminal approvals required for a bulk cargo marine terminal business; NOW, THEREFORE, the following resolutions are adopted: 1. SHARE CAPITAL AND SUBSCRIPTION. RESOLVED, that the authorized capital of the Company shall consist of [ ] shares of no par value; that [ ] shares have been validly issued and fully paid; that the full paid-in capital of [ ] Korean Won has been deposited into the provisional bank account in the name of the Company; and that the directors shall retain on file the certificate of deposit and contribution inspection report, where applicable, for incorporation registration. 2. REGISTERED OFFICE. RESOLVED, that the registered office of the Company shall be located at [ADDRESS], Republic of Korea, and that the landlord consent, registered-address extract, and a certified copy of the lease agreement shall be submitted to the District Court registry together with the incorporation application. 3. STATUTORY OFFICERS. RESOLVED, that the following persons shall serve until the next annual general meeting: [NAME] as Representative Director and Chief Executive Officer, [NAME] as Director, and [NAME] as Auditor to the extent an auditor is required by applicable law. Each director shall have authority to act within the limits of the Commercial Act and the Company's articles, and the Representative Director is specifically authorized to execute and file all incorporation documents, tax registrations, certificate-of-seal applications, and port-related permit applications. 4. BANKING AUTHORIZATION. RESOLVED, that bank account [ACCOUNT NUMBER] opened at [BANK NAME] shall be the principal operating account of the Company; that all checks, wire transfers, and payment instructions shall require either the joint signature of the Representative Director with one other Director, or the single signature of the Representative Director for payments below [THRESHOLD]; and that the bank shall be furnished with a certified copy of this resolution, the corporate seal registration certificate, and the certificate of incorporation upon issuance. 5. FURTHER ACTION. RESOLVED, that the executive officers are authorized and directed: to file the incorporation registration with the competent District Court; to file the business registration with the National Tax Service; to apply for the stevedoring business license under the Harbor Transportation Business Act; to execute the port facility lease and terminal operating agreement with the port authority; to engage an environmental consultant and to prepare or submit the environmental impact assessment if required; to obtain fire safety, civil defense, and occupational safety clearances; and to take all further actions necessary to carry out these resolutions. THIS WRITTEN RESOLUTION is effective as the first board resolution of the Company and shall be retained in the corporate minute book. ADOPTED this [ ] day of [ ] by the unanimous consent of the board of directors.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name availability check, notarization of Articles of Incorporation and deposit of paid-in capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Korean notary public; commercial registration name-search service operated by the Supreme Court of Korea; commercial bank selected for the provisional paid-in capital account.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Search the electronic commercial registration database to confirm the proposed corporate name does not conflict with any existing registered trade name. Prepare or revise the Articles of Incorporation to state the corporate purpose, registered office location, authorized and issued shares, share denomination, method of public notice, and initial directors. Each promoter or appointed representative must execute the articles; if a promoter executes outside Korea, the executed signature must be notarized and apostilled. The articles must then be notarized by a Korean notary public. After notarization, open a provisional account in the name of the company or the promoter for incorporation purposes, deposit the full subscription price, and obtain the bank certificate of paid-in capital. This step must be completed before submitting the incorporation registration application to the District Court.
required_dossiers: Passport or national identity document of each promoter and director
Apostilled certificate of incorporation or nationality evidence for foreign entities or individuals
Draft or final Articles of Incorporation
Notarized power of attorney if a representative signs on behalf of promoters
Certificate of Korean corporate name search
Bank account opening application and proof of deposit
Certificate of paid-in capital deposit
Corporate seal application or confirmed seal impression form
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the corporate name is rejected, select an alternative name and resubmit the search; if the notary raises a defect, correct the inconsistency in the articles and re-notarize before submission. If the bank rejects the provisional account opening, resolve the identity verification deficiency and provide an apostilled passport or foreign registration card, then reopen the account.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Commercial registration of incorporation at the District Court
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial Registration Office of the competent District Court, operating under the National Court Administration of the Supreme Court of Korea.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the Application for Registration of Incorporation of a Stock Company within two weeks from the date all shares are fully paid or the final in-kind contribution is completed. Attach the notarized Articles of Incorporation, certificate of paid-in capital deposit, instrument of contribution inspection if in-kind contributions exist, written consent forms of the initial directors and auditor, statement of first board resolution, and proof of registration surtax and court fee payment. The applicant must confirm that the actual principal office is within the court's territorial jurisdiction and that the lease contract is signed. The court will examine legal formalities and issue the Certificate of Registration of Incorporation, which marks the completion of the company's legal existence. The registered office address, corporate seal registration, and all newly appointed statutory officers must then be reflected in the court's public registry.
required_dossiers: Application for Registration of Incorporation of a Stock Company
Notarized Articles of Incorporation
Certificate of paid-in capital deposit
Record of promoters' incorporation meeting or shareholders' initial resolutions
Written consent to appointment of directors and auditor
Inspection report for in-kind contributions, if applicable
Power of attorney for the corporate formation attorney or agent
Certificate of lease and landlord consent for registered office
Copy of corporate seal registration application
Registration surtax and court fee payment receipts
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues a supplemental order, cure the cited defects and submit the missing documents within the stated period. If the registry refuses to accept the filing, request written confirmation of the reason, amend the application, re-file, and, if necessary, seek administrative review before the court or challenge through administrative litigation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Business registration with the National Tax Service
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local District Tax Office of the National Tax Service having jurisdiction over the registered office, filing via the HomeTaxService online portal or in-person window.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After incorporation, apply for corporate business registration to obtain the corporate identification number for value-added tax and corporate income tax purposes. Submit the certificate of incorporation registration, Articles of Incorporation, lease agreement, bank account confirmation, and representative director identification. The application must include the tax office jurisdiction, business establishment date, industry code for cargo handling and port stevedoring, and registered office address. The National Tax Service will issue the business registration certificate and assign a taxation number. Concurrently, if the Company will have employees or engage stevedores, register as an employer for withholding, national pension, health insurance, and industrial accident compensation insurance through the relevant public insurance institutions.
required_dossiers: Certificate of incorporation registration issued by the District Court
Notarized Articles of Incorporation
Corporate business registration application form
Lease contract or proof of registered office occupancy
Bank account certificate showing the corporate account
Passport or resident certificate of the Representative Director
Certificate of corporate seal registration
Foreign shareholder and director identification documents
Company bank account statement or certificate of bank balance
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax office places the application in suspense due to incomplete address evidence, provide a revised lease certificate or utility bill in the company's name. If the assigned tax office is incorrect, apply for transfer of jurisdiction or file an electronic correction through the HomeTaxService before receiving the registration certificate.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Stevedoring business license and port terminal operating approval
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries (MOF) through the Regional Maritime Affairs and Fisheries Office having jurisdiction over the port; Korea Port Authority or municipal port authority as the port facility lessor.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the application for a Stevedoring Business License under Article 5 of the Harbor Transportation Business Act. The application must include a business plan covering bulk cargo volumes, operational equipment, quayside or pier lease arrangements, labor deployment, ship winch and crane operations, emergency response, and port safety procedures. For use of public port facilities, execute a port facility lease or obtain permission from the port authority for operation of the bulk terminal. The license review will examine the applicant's financial solvency, operational capacity, cargo handling facilities, safety management plan, and compliance with environmental and port management requirements. The MOF may impose conditions concerning manpower qualifications, equipment registration, dust suppression, cargo residue disposal, and accident reporting. The license must be obtained before beginning commercial stevedoring operations.
required_dossiers: Stevedoring business license application form
Certificate of business registration from the National Tax Service
Certificate of incorporation registration
Articles of Incorporation and corporate seal certificate
Port facility lease agreement or terminal use permission
Bulk cargo handling business plan and volume forecasts
Equipment inventory and registration certificates for cranes or conveyor systems
Port operation and safety management manual
Certificates of professional qualifications for cargo handling supervisors
Financial statements or bank reference certificate
Cargo and equipment insurance policies
Emergency response and oil/chemical spill response plan
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If MOF requests supplemental submissions, provide the missing data within the prescribed period, usually 30 days. If the license is denied, file a written objection with MOF, request administrative reconsideration through the Central Administrative Appeals Commission, and, if necessary, initiate an administrative lawsuit in the relevant Administrative Court. If the port facility lease is contested, negotiate alternative berth or terminal allocation with the port authority and amend the business plan accordingly.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Fire safety, occupational health, and environmental operational clearances
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Fire Agency through the local Fire Station; Korea Occupational Safety and Health Agency (KOSHA); Ministry of Environment; local municipal government for construction and neighborhood safety.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the terminal facility drawings and obtain a Fire Safety Certificate under the Act on Fire Prevention, Firefighting and Disaster Management before commencing terminal operations. The local fire station will inspect fire extinguishing systems, hydrant flow, hazardous cargo storage zones, escape routes, and emergency lighting. Separately, submit the Occupational Safety and Health Plan and workplace risk assessment to KOSHA, including procedures for working in cargo holds, confined spaces, heavy equipment operation, and dust-generating bulk handling. If the bulk terminal involves new construction, reclamation, dredging, or wharf expansion, submit the Environmental Impact Assessment or simplified environmental review to the Ministry of Environment and obtain approval. Existing-terminal operators must file an environmental management plan and establish discharge and dust monitoring points as may be required by the local environmental office.
required_dossiers: Fire safety certificate application and building plans
Fire-fighting equipment specification sheets and hydraulic calculations
Hazardous cargo storage layout and material safety data sheets
Civil defense and emergency evacuation plan
Occupational Safety and Health Plan
Workplace risk assessment and confined-space entry permits
Crane and cargo-handling equipment inspection certificates
Structural load certificate for piers, quays, and silos
Environmental impact assessment report or environmental review application, if triggered
Wastewater discharge monitoring plan and sampling locations
Fugitive dust suppression plan and water nozzle layout
Hazardous waste carrier contracts and electronic manifest registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the fire station issues non-compliance findings, carry out corrective work and request re-inspection. If KOSHA imposes provisional suspension, submit a corrective action report and obtain approval before resuming work. If the Ministry of Environment requires a supplementary EIA, commission an environmental consultant to prepare supplemental studies and resubmit within the agency-specified deadline. Any denial may be appealed through the administrative review and administrative litigation route within statutory limitation periods.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries (MOF) and the Regional Maritime Affairs and Fisheries Office having jurisdiction over the port; Korea Port Authority or local port authority for terminal leasing and supervision; Ministry of Environment for environmental assessment.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Stevedoring Business License under Article 5 of the Harbor Transportation Business Act, together with Port Cargo Handling Terminal Operation Permit and Port Facility Lease under the Harbor Act.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Environment of the Republic of Korea, supported by the Korea Environment Corporation and coordinated with the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries through the Marine Environment Information System.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Full EIA Report under the Environmental Impact Assessment Act is required for the construction of a new bulk terminal, wharf expansion, reclamation, or dredging. Simplified Environmental Review applies to a small-scale terminal modification or extension within an existing port. Pure stevedoring operations using existing terminal infrastructure without new construction, dredging, or reclamation are eligible for an exemption from the formal EIA, but the operator must still register an environmental management plan and comply with fugitive dust and wastewater requirements.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater from terminal operations, washing, and maintenance areas must meet Water Environment Conservation Act effluent standards of BOD not exceeding 10 mg/L, COD (Mn) not exceeding 40 mg/L, suspended solids not exceeding 15 mg/L, total nitrogen not exceeding 20 mg/L, total phosphorus not exceeding 2 mg/L, and pH within 5.8 to 8.6. Point-source particulate matter discharge from combustion or dryers must not exceed 30 mg/Sm3, and NOx from diesel generators must not exceed 200 ppm at reference conditions. Fugitive dust from coal, ore, grain, or cement handling must not produce visible emissions beyond the terminal boundary, and cargo piles must be maintained with a moisture content and cover regime approved by the environmental authority. VOC emissions from maintenance and degreasing operations, if applicable, must be abated by activated carbon or equivalent technology so that total VOC concentration at the discharge point is below 500 mg/Sm3. Hazardous waste must be transported by a licensed carrier, manifested electronically through the KIHEC Waste Control System, and delivered only to licensed treatment and disposal facilities.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Civil Defense Fire Permit under the Act on Fire Prevention, Firefighting and Disaster Management, issued by the local Fire Service Headquarters after inspection of hydrants, extinguishing systems, escape routes, fire doors, and hazardous cargo receiving areas; structural safety and load-capacity inspection of quay cranes, conveyor trestles, silos, and pier decking by a registered structural engineer; Occupational Safety and Health clearance from KOSHA for bulk cargo handling, vessel mooring, confined-space entry, dust exposure, and heavy equipment operations; and, if hazardous quantities of dangerous substances are stored, a Dangerous Materials Storage Permit and separate emergency response approval from the local fire authority.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of the Republic of Korea; electronic portal: HomeTax. Korea Customs Service administers the UNI-PASS import/export clearance portal for customs and trade records.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a foreign non-resident entity establishing a Korean taxable footprint, the statutory procedure is to file a business registration application with the district tax office via HomeTax within 20 days of business commencement. The applicant must submit the certificate of incorporation, articles of incorporation, corporate registration certificate, proof of the Korean place of business, director identification and, for foreign non-resident principals, a domestic tax representative appointment letter. The NTS issues a 10-digit Business Registration Number that simultaneously constitutes the corporate TIN, corporate income tax identifier, and VAT registration number. A foreign entity without a Korean place of business that nevertheless makes VAT-taxable digital or other supplies in Korea must obtain a Korean VAT registration through the HomeTax electronic portal; where no Korean establishment is created, a domestic tax representative is mandatory. The port stevedoring business must first satisfy the applicable Korean maritime port cargo-handling/service provider licensing requirement before tax registration, and the registered domestic business address will be the place of supply and VAT collection posting point.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. The Republic of Korea has no check-the-box regime analogous to the United States and no elective hybrid-mismatch classification mechanism. A Chusik Hoesa is mandatorily taxable as a resident corporation under the Corporate Tax Act; any consolidated corporate taxation available under Korean law is a statutory group taxation regime, not an entity classification election.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-Added Tax (VAT) under the Value-Added Tax Act of the Republic of Korea, administered by the National Tax Service.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: KRW 80,000,000 annual taxable turnover is the simplified taxpayer threshold for small businesses, but it does not excuse a port terminal stevedoring Chusik Hoesa from mandatory VAT registration. A business with a Korean place of business is required to register upon commencement of a taxable business, regardless of turnover; a foreign non-resident supplier with a fixed place of business or any other VAT-nexus-creating supply in Korea is likewise required to register through HomeTax.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Electronic tax invoicing through the NTS HomeTax system is mandatory. Every VAT invoice issued by a registered business to another business must be an electronic tax invoice transmitted to the NTS with the statutory invoice number assigned by the system. For export and cross-border trade flows, the Korea Customs Service UNI-PASS portal operates electronic export/import clearance, requiring data exchange with shipping agents and the NTS. Korea does not maintain a separate digital fiscal stamp, stamp duty, or receipt-stamping system for ordinary VAT; the anti-fraud control is embedded in the mandatory real-time electronic invoice transmission and customs clearance records.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under Article 24 of the Value-Added Tax Act, goods physically exported from Korea are zero-rated where the customs export declaration, shipment documentation and foreign exchange receipt substantiate the export. Qualifying services related to international trade, including stevedoring and bulk cargo loading/unloading services provided for goods exported through a Korean port, may be zero-rated if the service is supplied in the course of or incidental to the export of such goods and the consideration is collected in a manner consistent with the VAT Enforcement Decree. Port services connected with domestic cargo or with import clearance of goods into Korea remain subject to VAT at the standard rate.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: UNI-PASS electronic Export Declaration (export clearance confirmation with export declaration number)
Commercial invoice, packing list and weight list
Bill of Lading (B/L) or equivalent multimodal transport document showing the cargo destined from a Korean port to a foreign place
Certificate of receipt of export proceeds issued by a licensed Korean foreign exchange bank evidencing settlement in foreign currency
Terminal stevedoring contract, work order and service completion certificate covering the bulk port handling operation
Cargo manifest/terminal tally sheet or container record matching the loading operation to the export declaration
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The National Tax Service and Korea Customs Service may audit the linkage between the customs export declaration, bill of lading, terminal service records and foreign exchange remittance evidence. If zero-rating is not substantiated, or invoices or customs documents are false or fictitious, the NTS will claw back the zero rate and assess the 10% VAT plus statutory additional taxes for failure to report, underreporting and late payment, with penalty interest running until payment. Deliberately fraudulent export zero-rating or fabricated stevedoring/customs documentation is subject to criminal sanctions under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act and the Customs Act, including imprisonment and fines, and the responsible directors or Korean tax representative may be jointly liable for the unpaid tax and penalties.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Korea (BOK), supported by the Ministry of Economy and Finance (MOEF) and the Foreign Exchange Information System (FEIS) as the regulatory backbone under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: KRW is a managed floating currency with current account transactions largely liberalised under Article 4 / 5 of the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act. Import/export trade settlement and service payments can pass through a licensed foreign exchange bank after submission of underlying contracts, invoices, and customs documents. Capital account transactions, including foreign direct investment (FDI), securities investment, loans, and derivatives, are subject to either advance declaration, approval, or post-settlement reporting to the Bank of Korea through the Foreign Exchange Information System (FEIS). There is no overnight surrender ratio for export proceeds, but foreign currency earnings must be retained in a domestic foreign exchange account or sold to a licensed bank within allowed settlement periods. Profit remittances to non-resident shareholders are current account transactions if the entity produces audited financial statements, tax clearance certificates, and board dividend resolutions; however the bank may apply a currency conversion screening for excessive cash sweeps or round-tripping. Non-resident won accounts are closely watched and offshore won clearing is disconnected from domestic transfer rails, so convertibility is ultimately conditional on KYC, tax status, and underlying economic substance. For a port stevedoring terminal, tariff receivables from non-resident owners, equipment imports, and dividend payments require an unbroken paper trail and FEIS filing; there is no meaningful unofficial parallel market for KRW.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Mandatory conversion ratio: 0%. Statutory timeline: export proceeds must be collected through a Korean foreign exchange bank and reported to FEIS within 180 days of the export declaration date, unless a longer credit period is approved in advance by the Ministry of Economy and Finance or notified via the relevant foreign exchange bank. If not converted to KRW, the full amount must be credited to a domestic foreign currency account at a Korean bank; conversion at the bank is permitted for qualifying import settlements, external debt repayments, or dividend payments. Any failure to bring proceeds into Korea or to report settlement is treated as an unrepatriated export collection and may trigger a foreign exchange audit.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account (Foreign Investment Capital Deposit)
Capital Escrow Account (Foreign Investment Capital Deposit)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low. Offshore digital EMIs and cross-border payment fintechs are structurally barred from acting as the primary settlement bank for a Korean Chusik Hoesa because only licensed domestic foreign exchange banks may execute KRW settlement, receive foreign investment capital, handle export proceeds, or clear outbound FX payments under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act. An EMI could only be used for pre-onboarding expense logistics or as a non-ledger coordination tool, and all actual treasury transactions must be routed through a tier-one Korean bank. Using an EMI without a Korean foreign exchange bank licence would create unlawful foreign exchange dealing, expose the entity to FEIS penalties, and break the capital verification chain required by the Foreign Investment Promotion Act.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Korean financial institutions enforce the Financial Transaction Real Name Act and FATF-aligned AML rules. A newly formed Chusik Hoesa foreign director must normally attend in-branch on a business day for a face-to-face identity and beneficial ownership interview and provide original corporate documents in Korean or apostilled and notarised translations. Remote opening is not standard; some banks accept a consular-authenticated general power of attorney authorising a domestic resident or external local agent to appear in-branch, combined with a real-time video interview and second-line compliance approval. Pure remote or consular proxy opening without any in-country bank interview is generally prohibited.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: UBO chain opacity where the Chusik Hoesa is jointly held by foreign and Korean investors with nominee or shelf structure
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified corporate register, share ledger, UBO declaration, passport or ID copies for each natural person holding 25% or more, source-of-wealth documentation, audited investor financial statements, and a corporate resolution identifying the ultimate controller with an organisational chart.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Mismatch between the stevedoring terminal business and the initial capital contribution or rapid liquidity inflows
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Port authority licence or concession agreement, legalised business plan, equipment procurement proformas, actual cargo throughput contracts with shippers, board-approved funding plan, and bank confirmation of foreign investment capital receipts.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions and vessel ownership red flags in bulk cargo trade with charterers from high-risk jurisdictions
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Vessel IMO level sanctions screening against OFAC, EU, and UN lists, charter party and bill of lading, cargo origin certificate, beneficial cargo owner declaration, adverse media check, ship vetting report, and a written trade compliance policy.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Potential diversion of export proceeds or unreported settlement through an offshore account
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Korean customs export declarations, FEIS settlement records, bank transaction statements, collection advice from freight forwarders, outstanding aging report, and auditor confirmation letter linking each settlement to an invoice or charter party.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: All inbound equity injections must be wired by SWIFT MT103 from the foreign investor's licensed bank to a newly opened foreign investment capital deposit account at a Korean designated foreign exchange bank. The remittance message must reference the Foreign Investment Promotion Act investment report number and the investor's full legal name. After the bank receives the funds, it registers the capital arrival, converts the foreign currency into KRW at the market rate, deposits into the company operating account, and files the declaration with FEIS. Capital verification is completed by the bank issuing a foreign investment capital remittance certificate and by the statutory auditor confirming the investment against the board resolution. No crypto, non-bank payment token, or third-party unofficial settlement is permissible.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound disbursements for stevedoring and terminal operations should use SWIFT MT103 for fee and operational payments such as port authority charges, wages, fuel, and equipment purchase; Commercial Letters of Credit for imported terminal machinery and bulk handling equipment; and Documentary Collections for moderate-risk purchases from known suppliers. Each remittance requires an underlying contract, invoice, tax invoice, and customs declaration; the domestic bank screens against FEIS and ensures the settlement is classified under the correct BOK foreign exchange transaction purpose code. Korean won clearing with domestic port authorities uses domestic demand deposit transfer rails, while cross-border payments must be denominated in a permitted foreign currency unless a non-resident invoicing exemption applies.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore KRW/USD and KRW/major-currency forward contracts with a Korean foreign exchange bank, limited to the amount and duration of actual receivable or payable exposure from terminal tariffs, stevedoring contracts, or equipment supply, and recorded under hedge accounting documentation.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) only through an authorised domestic foreign exchange bank or permitted offshore dealer where BOK/MOEF actual-demand exemption exists; not permitted for speculative positions or uncovered exposure.

Cross-currency and interest-rate swaps are permissible only for long-term project finance liabilities tied to FIPA-registered FDI debt and port infrastructure capex, subject to board treasury policy, FEIS reporting, and no leverage creation.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax Return including Local Corporate Income Tax Surtax Return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service of South Korea; local corporate income tax is remitted through the same NTS electronic system to the competent Metropolitan City or Province tax authority
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By the last day of the third month following the business year-end; for a calendar-year Chusik Hoesa, 31 March; a one-month extension to 30 April is available if the return is prepared by a certified tax accountant or a licensed accountant
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing surtax of 20% of the unpaid corporate tax; under-reporting surtax of 10%; fraudulent or off-book omission surtax of 40%; late-payment interest accrues at 0.022% per day on the unpaid national and local corporate tax; persistent delinquency triggers seizure of bank accounts, receivables, equipment and vessel-asset liens, refusal of tax clearance certificates, and administrative strike-off or judicial dissolution for a dormant company.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Semi-Annual Value-Added Tax Net Returns for the two half-year taxable periods
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service of South Korea, respective district tax office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: First half-year period covering 1 January to 30 June is due 25 July; second half-year period covering 1 July to 31 December is due 25 January of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing penalty equal to 20% of the relevant output value-added tax; false or excessive refund return penalty of 10%, escalated to 40% for fraudulent transactions; unpaid tax interest accrues at 0.022% per day; repeated non-filing can cancel zero-rating or export VAT refund eligibility and escalate to tax summons, business closure notice, and collection liens against the stevedoring terminal equipment.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Periodic General Shareholders' Meeting with approval of annual financial statements, dividend resolution and board report
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Internal corporate organ of the Chusik Hoesa; minutes are kept at the registered head office and no filing fee or state registry fee applies
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Must be convened and resolved within three months after the end of each business year under Article 365 of the Korean Commercial Act; for calendar-year companies this means by 31 March unless the articles of incorporation provide a special convention date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to convene within the statutory period is a commercial-law defect; resolutions adopted at a later meeting remain valid but responsible directors may be subject to administrative fines under Article 635 of the Korean Commercial Act, and dissenting shareholders may petition a court to order the summons of the meeting; unapproved financial statements also render the next period's audit opinion qualified.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Independent Certified Public Auditor's Report and audited financial statements filing under the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Supervisory Service of South Korea through DART electronic disclosure system; copy of the audit report is also furnished to the National Tax Service for the corporate tax dossier where the company is an audit-target entity
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For audit-subject companies, the auditor's report must be filed with FSS within two weeks after delivery of the report by the auditor; the audited annual financial statements must be submitted to the annual general meeting before the end of the three-month AGM deadline; where the company is a listed or publicly disclosing corporation, the DART annual business report is due within 90 days after fiscal year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to appoint an external auditor is punishable by administrative fines under the External Audit Act and may subject directors to statutory penalties; failure to file the audit report with FSS triggers fines, public announcement of audit-related deficiencies, and adverse qualification disclosures; in port concession financing, a qualified or adverse audit opinion may constitute a loan covenant default leading to accelerated repayment or concession termination.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual commercial-registry occurrence reports, shareholder-ledger confirmation, foreign-investor alteration filing and business-activity evidence
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Korean Commercial Registry, competent district court; National Tax Service Business Registration Office; Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy/KOTRA for foreign-invested ownership changes
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No general Korean franchise annual return exists; however, registration-required events must be filed within two weeks of the event for corporate representation changes and within 30 days after any foreign-invested share transfer under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act; dormant companies must submit tax-operation evidence each annual tax filing to maintain active business registration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late commercial registration fines are determined by the district court and are typically minor; unregistered directors or unregistered de facto managers can jeopardize limited-liability defenses and equity claims; continuous failure to submit tax returns or business-operation evidence can lead to cancellation of business registration, loss of tax clearance, and judicial dissolution or administrative strike-off where the company has been inactive for three consecutive years.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies, a Chusik Hoesa must engage an independent CPA auditor if total assets on the balance sheet at the end of the immediately preceding business year equal or exceed KRW 12 billion, approximately USD 9.1 million at an exchange rate of 1,320 KRW/USD. There is no separate turnover or headcount threshold for an ordinary non-listed bulk stevedoring company; however, audit is also mandated if the company is a listed corporation or publicly disclosing company under the Financial Investment Services and Capital Markets Act, if it is a financial institution or public-interest company designated by Presidential Decree, if it is subject to a mandate from the Securities and Futures Commission for investor protection, or if it is the parent of a group that must prepare consolidated K-IFRS statements because one or more subsidiaries meet the same asset threshold. Port-terminal licensees subject to the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries financial capacity review may be required to provide audited financial statements even when the statutory audit threshold is not met.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: K-IFRS (Korean International Financial Reporting Standards) is obligatory for listed companies and the standard financial reporting framework for most audit-subject companies; non-listed audit-target companies may apply K-GAAP (Korean Generally Accepted Accounting Principles) under the Act on External Audit and the Korean Accounting Standards Board codification; small non-audit companies may keep tax-basis accrual books under the Corporate Income Tax Act, but once an external audit is triggered, the financial statements and notes must present stevedoring revenue, demurrage, terminal equipment depreciation and port concession liabilities in conformity with K-IFRS or K-GAAP.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: South Korea does not maintain a separate annual UBO filing for ordinary private Chusik Hoesa. The company must keep a current shareholder ledger and, whenever shareholding or control changes, update the ledger and supporting board minutes. For foreign-invested companies, a share-transfer alteration report must be filed with the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy/KOTRA within 30 days of the transfer that changes foreign ownership percentage. Under Korean AML/FATF rules, the company must collect, refresh and retain real beneficial owner information in the customer due diligence records applicable to port-authority clearing and SWIFT wire accounts; a 30-day record-update protocol is applied upon any direct shareholding change or any material control change by an existing shareholder. Quoted or large disclosing companies separately file substantial-shareholding reports with the Financial Supervisory Service; private closed companies confirm beneficial ownership indirectly through the annual corporate tax return beneficial-ownership declaration and the shareholder ledger presented at the annual general meeting.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (Shareholders Ledger including share classes, number of shares, transfer dates and paid-in amount)
Register of Directors (current directors, statutory auditor, audit committee members and representation authority)
Register of Charges/Mortgages (share pledge register and asset charges or floating charges if any)
Minute Book of General Meetings and Board of Directors Meetings

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 800 - USD 2,300 per year for standard Seoul or Busan corporate secretarial and registered-office services; higher for marine terminal cities requiring physical presence and vessel-related document handling.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 0 if no statutory audit is triggered; if the Chusik Hoesa is an audit-target company, typical certified audit fees range from USD 8,000 to USD 24,000 depending on total assets, port terminal equipment size, subsidiaries and international transactions.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 9% for taxable income up to KRW 200 million; 19% for taxable income above KRW 200 million and up to KRW 20 billion; 21% for taxable income above KRW 20 billion and up to KRW 300 billion; 24% for taxable income above KRW 300 billion (exclusive of the 10% local income tax surcharge, making the aggregate headline burden 9.9%, 20.9%, 23.1% and 26.4% respectively).
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: The Chusik Hoesa may benefit from targeted incentives under the Restriction of Special Taxation Act, including the R&D expense tax credit, temporary facility investment credit, job creation credit, duty drawback and FEZ/free trade port corporate tax reductions for foreign-invested enterprises; there is no automatic patent box for stevedoring, but capital-intensive port cranes, conveyor systems and automated bulk handling equipment may qualify for accelerated depreciation and investment tax credits under the National Tax Basic Act and RSTA.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Primary corporate income tax return: the Corporate Tax Base and Tax Return (the statutory annual corporate income tax return of the Republic of Korea) with attached financial statements, tax adjustment schedules, international transactions report, transfer pricing disclosure and the local income tax surcharge schedule; filed electronically through the National Tax Service HomeTax e-filing portal (www.hometax.go.kr).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; the final annual return is filed once for each fiscal year, and non-resident dividend, interest and royalty withholding returns are filed intermittently on the dates of remittance or on a quarterly remittance schedule.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The annual corporate tax return must be filed on or before the last day of the third month following the fiscal year-end; for a December 31 fiscal year-end the return is due by March 31 of the next calendar year; electronic filing and certified tax representative review may extend the deadline by one additional month, but interest and daily surcharges continue to accrue on any unpaid tax.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal identity and fiscal period: business registration number, corporate name, head office address, representative director, tax office, fiscal year beginning and ending dates, and ownership structure.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the Korean Chusik Hoesa business registration number exactly as registered. If a foreign parent is a shareholder, attach the foreign investment registration certificate and disclose non-resident ownership percentage. Non-resident shareholders are not listed individually on this line unless they are legal representatives, but the corporate register, board minutes and share transfer records must be maintained to substantiate treaty relief and to calculate dividend withholding.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross income and sales revenue: stevedoring fees, cargo handling charges, bulk loading and unloading fees, wharfage, storage and throughput fees, demurrage billings, dispatch refunds, and incidental dock-side logistic services.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Recognize revenue under K-IFRS or K-GAAP on the accrual basis. For services physically performed in Korean ports for foreign ocean carriers, all revenue attributable to Korean stevedoring operations must be included in the Korean tax base. If a foreign client contractually opts for a net-of-withholding-tax price, gross-up the invoice amount into Box 2 revenue. Exclusion of Korean-source wharfage or demurrage from the return is a common audit trigger that produces underreporting penalties.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductible expenses: stevedoring labor costs, crane and conveyor depreciation, equipment leases, fuel, electricity, port concession fees, terminal maintenance, marine insurance, pollution control, repairs, officer compensation and administrative overhead.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Deductions must be supported by Korean tax invoices, payroll records, bank wire evidence and signed contracts. Expenses paid to non-resident related parties, such as group management fees, technical service fees, charter hire and headquarters allocations, are deductible only to the extent they are arm's length, actually performed, and supported by contemporaneous documentation. Non-deductible items include entertainment expense in excess of statutory limits, foreign corporate income taxes, and illegal political contributions. Intercompany interest is further limited by the thin capitalization rule under the International Tax Adjustment Act.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income before loss carryforward: gross income less deductible expenses plus mandatory tax adjustments for non-deductible items and temporary differences.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach the tax adjustment schedule and reconcile book income to tax income. Items commonly adjusted for a port terminal include depreciation differences on heavy equipment, allowance for doubtful accounts, severance reserve, and disallowed entertainment expenses. The adjustment schedule must be signed by the representative director; a false tax adjustment schedule that understates Korean taxable income is a direct basis for a criminal tax fraud referral.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductible carried-forward losses: the aggregate net operating losses of prior fiscal years that remain within the statutory carryforward period and have not yet been deducted.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach a year-by-year loss carryforward schedule with original tax return confirmation. Korean tax law permits a 10-year carryforward period for most corporations and 15 years for small and medium enterprises. No carryforward is allowed for losses attributable to tax haven businesses or where the entity failed to file the underlying return. Amended returns must be filed before the statute of limitations expires to preserve the loss inventory.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporate income tax base: taxable income before deducting losses less deductible carried-forward losses and any authorized exemption/reduction amount.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Round the tax base down to the nearest KRW 1,000. Any tax exemption for foreign-invested enterprises in a free economic zone or free trade port must be pre-approved by the relevant authority; an unauthorized reduction in Box 6 is treated as fraudulent underreporting and subject to the 40% penalty for fraudulent returns.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computed corporate income tax: application of the progressive rates in Article 55 of the Corporate Tax Act to the Box 6 tax base.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the marginal rate brackets separately: 9% on the first KRW 200 million; 19% on the next bracket; 21% on the next bracket; and 24% on income above KRW 300 billion. A Korean resident Chusik Hoesa is taxed on worldwide income; non-resident ownership does not change the rate computation. Compute the 10% local income tax surcharge separately and carry it to the local income tax schedule.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax credits and reductions: R&D credits, facility investment credits, job creation credits, employment-oriented tax reduction, tax credit for foreign taxes paid, and RSTA exemption/reduction for foreign-invested enterprises.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign tax credits are available only with treaty or statute support and must be claimed with a Form 40 supporting schedule evidencing the foreign tax actually paid on Korean-source income. Investment credits for port equipment must be claimed in the year the asset is placed in service; late claims are disallowed. If the entity is owned by a non-resident through an intermediate jurisdiction, no tax credit is allowed for tax paid by the intermediate parent itself.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Additional tax and penalties: underreporting surcharge, unfaithful return surcharge, late filing surcharge, daily late payment surcharge, delinquency interest, and the additional tax for failure to file or misstating the international transactions report.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include the 10% local income tax surcharge on the Article 55 corporate tax. If the taxpayer files a timely but erroneous return, penalties are 10% of the negligent understated tax or 40% of the fraudulent understated tax; late payment interest accrues at the statutory rate from the original due date. Failure to attach the international transactions report triggers a separate additional tax of up to 3% of the undisclosed related-party transaction amount and may invalidate the ability to claim treaty relief.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net tax payable or refund: total corporate tax plus local surcharge plus additional tax, less intermediate prepayments, withholding credits and previously paid installments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Pay the net amount through HomeTax before the statutory deadline. If a non-resident shareholder subsequently declares a dividend from after-tax retained earnings, the dividend is not reported in this box; the Korean payer must separately withhold 22% (or treaty-reduced rate) on the dividend remittance and file a withholding return for the non-resident.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing attracts an unfaithful return surcharge of 10% for negligent underreporting and 40% for fraudulent underreporting under the Basic National Tax Act; a complete failure to file is subject to a 20% unpaid tax surcharge, plus a daily late payment surcharge of 0.03% of the unpaid tax for each day from the statutory deadline, plus statutory delinquency interest. Willful false filing or documentation of offshore profit stripping is prosecuted as tax fraud, with imprisonment and fines up to twice the evaded tax, and the National Tax Service may blacklist the representative and issue a travel ban pending full payment.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 22% aggregate statutory rate on outbound dividends to non-resident corporate shareholders: 20% corporate withholding tax under the Corporate Tax Act plus 10% local income tax surcharge on the withholding tax; treaty-reduced rates apply only after administrative relief is granted.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim reduced dividend, interest or royalty withholding under a bilateral tax treaty, the non-resident beneficial owner must file a treaty relief application with the Korean withholding agent or the National Tax Service before the payment date. The required package includes: (1) an original Tax Residency Certificate issued by the jurisdiction of residence for the calendar year of the payment, certifying the entity is a beneficial owner resident in that jurisdiction; (2) a beneficial ownership declaration and corporate structure chart showing direct shareholding, voting rights, and absence of pass-through or back-to-back obligations; (3) corporate constitutive documents and board resolutions evidencing legal capacity and actual control; (4) if a treaty requires a holding period for the reduced dividend rate, a statement and share register demonstrating continuous ownership; and (5) confirmation that the non-resident shareholder does not have a Korean permanent establishment attributable to the income. The NTS examines the application, may request additional substance documentation, and if denial results at source, the non-resident can pay the 22% withholding and pursue a refund under the mutual agreement procedure in the DTA.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory withholding on royalties and interest paid to non-residents is also 22% aggregate (20% withholding tax plus 10% local surtax). Depending on the applicable DTA, interest is generally reduced to 10% or less, and royalties are generally reduced to 15%, 10% or 0% for certain software and industrial, commercial or scientific equipment payments. Royalties for the use of port-terminal software, cargo handling technology, trademarks and know-how must satisfy the beneficial ownership and Korean-source income rules before treaty relief is available; the Korean tax treaty allows the NTS to deny treaty benefits when the intermediary lacks economic substance.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: KRW 10,000,000,000 in annual international related-party transactions for a mandatory Local File; a Master File is required when the multinational enterprise group has consolidated annual revenue of at least KRW 1,000,000,000,000 and the Korean Chusik Hoesa is a participating group entity; a Country-by-Country Report is required at the group level for consolidated revenue above the KRW 1 trillion threshold.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Korea has no GCC-style Economic Substance Regulations by that exact name, but the substance over form principle under the Basic National Tax Act and the general anti-abuse rule allow the tax authority to disregard a corporate vehicle that lacks genuine economic operations. A Korea Chusik Hoesa operating a bulk port stevedoring terminal must perform its Core Income-Generating Activities in Korea: employment of stevedoring labor, operation of cranes and cargo handling equipment, maintenance of the port terminal concession, execution of service contracts, invoicing from Korean offices, and exercise of board-level management functions in Korea. A foreign-owned shell that merely invoices port services and relocates profits to a zero-tax jurisdiction without Korean employees, assets or decision-making will be recharacterized, denied treaty benefits, and the related-party transaction may be reconstructed as a dividend or capital contribution.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Corporate Tax Evasion and False Tax Return
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately omitting substantive stevedoring revenue from foreign ocean carriers, underreporting demurrage and wharfage receipts, fabricating invoices for non-existent sub-contractor costs, or filing a tax return that claims fictitious deductions for related-party service fees without arm's length proof.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Basic National Tax Act Articles 47-2 through 47-5, the tax authority imposes a 40% fraudulent underreporting surcharge on the additionally assessed tax, daily late payment surcharge of 0.03% per day, statutory delinquency interest, and criminal referral under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act Article 3; the offender may receive imprisonment for up to 3 years and a fine of up to twice the evaded tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The National Tax Service may pierce the corporate veil if the Chusik Hoesa is found to be a facade or conduit; directors are jointly and severally liable for unpaid corporate tax, and the representative director is blacklisted as a delinquent taxpayer, subject to a travel ban, asset seizure and compulsory examination. Criminal prosecution may result in personal imprisonment and a personal fine, and the director is disqualified from serving on any Korean corporate board for the duration of the criminal sanction.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Non-Resident Withholding Tax Evasion on Dividends, Interest and Royalties
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The Korean Chusik Hoesa pays dividends, interest on intercompany loans, or royalties for port technology to a non-resident parent, affiliated company or intermediary in a no-tax jurisdiction without withholding the statutory 22% and without filing a withholding return, while falsely claiming a treaty exemption without a Tax Residency Certificate or substantive beneficial ownership.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Corporate Tax Act and the Income Tax Act, the withholding agent becomes personally liable for the uncollected withholding tax and is additionally assessed a withholding penalty of 10% of the withheld amount where the failure to withhold is negligent, with daily surcharges and interest; if the non-payment exceeds the statutory threshold, the criminal provisions of the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act apply with imprisonment and fines.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The representative director and the finance director who authorized the wire remittance to the foreign payee are jointly liable for the withheld tax and penalties; the NTS attaches personal real estate and bank accounts, the director receives a travel ban, and a criminal conviction carries personal imprisonment of up to 3 years, with potential replacement of the corporate charter and revocation of the port terminal license for non-compliance.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Manipulation and Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The Korean terminal pays inflated management fees, phantom consulting charges, excessive charter hire or high-interest loans to a related foreign entity that has no employees, no offices, no risk and no functional control, thereby eroding the Korean stevedoring profit and misrepresenting the transaction in the international transactions report to avoid transfer pricing documentation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the International Tax Adjustment Act Articles 4-5 and 7, the National Tax Service recomputes the arm's length income, disallows the excess related-party payment, adds the amount to the Korean corporate tax base, and imposes transfer pricing penalties, international transactions report penalties of up to 3% of the undisclosed transaction amount, and general underreporting penalties of 40% for a fraudulent return, together with daily late payment surcharges and interest.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The directors who signed the false transfer pricing documentation and the Korean tax return are personally liable for the additional tax when the legal entity is a sham; the NTS applies the substance-over-form doctrine to deprive the corporate veil, aggregates personal and corporate assets, imposes a travel ban and blacklisting, and files criminal charges under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act for fraudulent tax evasion, carrying a sentence of imprisonment up to 3 years and a fine up to twice the evaded tax, with the court additionally ordering restitution of the national tax loss.
